destinations.heroTitle: Choose the city where your German year begins
destinations.heroSubtitle: DARB works with selected language and education institutions to help students build German language skills, experience life in Germany, and prepare for the next university step.
destinations.introBody: Your language year is more than a course. We help you choose a city and an institution that fit your route, then connect the year in Germany to your university preparation.
destinations.step1Body: Compare the pace, lifestyle and learning environment before deciding where to spend your year.
destinations.step2Body: Start from your current level and plan toward the German level and exam you need.
destinations.step3Body: Use your time outside class to experience the city, culture and student environment.
destinations.step4Body: Keep your language plan connected to your future university and major choices.
destinations.citiesTitle: Five cities. Five different ways to experience Germany
destinations.citiesBody: These are the cities currently featured in the DARB language-year pathway.
destinations.schoolsTitle: The institutions behind the language year
destinations.schoolsBody: We work with selected institutions and show their own qualifications and examination credentials openly. The labels below belong to the respective school or awarding body — not to DARB.
destinations.tu9Body: The language year is the preparation stage. From there, students can explore university options across Germany, including the nine TU9 member universities.
destinations.disclosureBody: DARB does not issue the certificates, quality marks or awards shown on this page. They identify the respective language school, examination centre, quality organisation or award body. Course places, exams and their terms remain subject to the institution's current rules.
destinations.endTitle: Not sure which city fits your plan?
destinations.endBody: Tell DARB what you want to study and where you are starting from. We can help you map the language year to your next step.

destinations.selectionTitle: A language year chosen around your university route
destinations.selectionBody: DARB looks at the practical pieces that matter for an international student: progression through German levels, exam access, academic preparation, student support, accommodation and the city itself.
destinations.selection1Body: The institution offers a clear route toward the language level or exam commonly needed for the next academic step.
destinations.selection2Body: Where available, official test-centre and preparation options are shown so you can plan the year realistically.
destinations.selection3Body: We look for practical support around accommodation, orientation, activities or arrival — not just classroom hours.
destinations.selection4Body: The place you live shapes the language year. We therefore show the city, transport and life around the school.

journey.title: A language year with the next step already in view

journey.stage6Body: Move from language preparation into the application stage for your next academic step.

educational.bagrutTitle: Bagrut units and how your average translates to a German grade
educational.bagrutUnits: Verified in anabin (record ISR-BV01): the Bagrut gives direct admission to all subjects at all German universities if it includes Mathematics at 3 units, English at 4 units and one further subject at 4 units. No other subject units are required nationwide.
educational.bagrutFormula: Conversion uses the KMK modified Bavarian formula: German grade = 1 + 3 × (100 − your average) ÷ (100 − {{min}}). 1.0 is the best grade, 4.0 the lowest pass.
educational.bagrutDisclaimer: Indicative only: the pass mark used for Israel in the official conversion is not publicly listed by anabin, and uni-assist or the university issues the binding conversion (VPD).
educational.sourcesDisclaimer: Admission requirements change by intake. Always confirm on the university's page before applying.
